draft.title: Function notation
card: f(x) is the output of the function f when the input is x. It is read as "f of x". It does not mean f multiplied by x.
To evaluate f(3), replace every x in the rule with 3. If f(x) = 2x² − 5, then f(3) = 2 × 3² − 5 = 2 × 9 − 5 = 13.
The input can be an expression. To find f(a + 1), put the whole bracket (a + 1) in place of x. For f(x) = 3x − 2, f(a + 1) = 3(a + 1) − 2 = 3a + 1.
A rule can be written in words and then in notation. "Double the input and add 4" is f(x) = 2x + 4.
draft.remember: To find f of something, put that something in place of every x.

a.why: Replace x with 5: f(5) = 4 × 5 − 7 = 20 − 7 = 13. The answer 20 comes from forgetting to subtract 7.
a.clue: Put 5 in place of x, then follow the order of operations.

b.q: If f(x) = x² + 2x, what is f(a + 1)?
b.why: f(a + 1) = (a + 1)² + 2(a + 1) = a² + 2a + 1 + 2a + 2 = a² + 4a + 3. The option a² + 2a + 3 comes from writing (a + 1)² as a² + 1, which skips the middle term.
b.clue: Put the whole bracket in place of x, then expand (a + 1)² fully.
